title: SEC-TESTS: bt5.5 epoch error path has no test
description: The fix for bt5.5 added error handling in validate_post_headers() / check_date() (reader/src/post/validate_headers.rs line 121): SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).map_err(|_| Response::new(441, 'Internal fault: system clock before Unix epoch')). There is no #[test] that exercises this specific error path. The code path is untestable directly because SystemTime::now() cannot return a pre-epoch time in a unit test without dependency injection or a test-only clock abstraction. However, the fix DOES change behavior: before the fix, the error would have been a panic or an unwrap; after the fix, it returns a 441 response. The test requirement is: verify that check_date() returns a 441 Response when given a timestamp delta that triggers the error, OR that the implementation never panics on clock failure. Oracle: the specific error message 'Internal fault: system clock before Unix epoch' and the 441 code are the defined expected values. A test using a known-future date that does not trigger clock_before_epoch but does verify the branch structure would be insufficient. Currently the error path has 0% test coverage.
